look_here_first: Look at the colored bracts, not just the flowers. Lindheimer's paintbrush is a perennial hemiparasite with narrow leaves, upper leaves often lobed, and a terminal spike whose three-lobed bracts turn orange-red to scarlet around the much less conspicuous tubular flowers.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial hemiparasitic herb, several-stemmed from the base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves alternate, narrow linear to lanceolate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: upper cauline leaves often divided into 2–3 narrow lobes

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: bract lobes orange-red to light scarlet

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: corolla strongly bilateral with beak-like upper lip

key_traits.label: Hemiparasite training
key_traits.text: Green photosynthetic plant that also forms root connections to neighboring hosts; do not interpret a single nearby grass in a still frame as proof of the exact host individual.
